advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add resign tests covering the `states`, `missing-child-state`, and `malformed` refusal branches of `_generation_child_states`, asserting the specific `child_impact_state_error["reason"]` (not just `event`) for each.
evidence: test_plan_review_resign.py:136 `@pytest.mark.parametrize("snapshot_kind", ["missing", "mismatched-child"])` covers only 2 of the 5 branches

test_plan_review_resign.py:181-183 asserts only `result["child_impact_state_error"]["event"] == "plan_review_child_impact_snapshot_invalid"` — `event` is identical for all five branches, so the assertion cannot distinguish a misclassified or collapsed `reason`

ABSENCE: no test feeds a snapshot whose `ticket_states_by_id` is not a dict, whose `child_ids` references a missing child, or whose `child_ids` is non-iterable — the ticket contract states 'Missing or inconsistent snapshot child state remains a structured refusal, never a broader or falsely narrow signature', so a regression that returned children (a falsely-narrow signature) instead of refusing on these malformed inputs would go undetected
advisory.finding: _generation_child_states produces five distinct structured-refusal `reason` values (missing, states, missing-child-state, child-id-mismatch, malformed) but only two branches (missing, child-id-mismatch) are exercised, and the single test asserts only the constant `event` field — never the distinguishing `reason`. The `states` (non-dict ticket_states_by_id), `missing-child-state` (child_id absent from states), and `malformed` (AttributeError/TypeError from a non-iterable child_ids) branches are entirely untested, and no test proves the refusal reason is classified correctly.
scenarios: A future edit reorders/merges the reason branches or lets a non-dict `ticket_states_by_id` fall through to signing
A malformed relation snapshot (non-iterable child_ids) that should refuse instead raises unhandled or produces a narrowed signature
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the `snapshot_kind` parametrization with cases for a non-dict `ticket_states_by_id`, a `child_ids` entry absent from `ticket_states_by_id`, and a snapshot whose `child_ids` is non-iterable (triggering TypeError), and assert `result["child_impact_state_error"]["reason"]` equals `"states"`, `"missing-child-state"`, and `"malformed"` respectively.

evidence: manifest.py:350 `if own_scope == "none" or (own_scope == "undeclared" and container_all_none):` returns "none"
manifest.py:310 `return _ChildImpact(frozenset(out), live_count > 0 and all_none)` — all_none is True for an all-"none"-children container with empty paths
attest.py:167 `file_scope=classify_file_scope(deps.keys(), own_scope, container_all_none=child_impact.all_none)` — new container path into "none"

attest.py:709 `elif manifest_file_scope(auth_manifest) != "none":` — the whole-HEAD stale-head fallback (lines 710-717) is SKIPPED when file_scope=="none" and deps is empty, so no code-drift check runs at all

attest.py:742 `if plan_health["enforced"] and plan_health["pin_status"] not in (...)` — child pin-drift (stale-pin-drift) only invalidates at validity time when enforced is true
_config_schema.py:233 `enforce_plan_material_pins: bool = False` — default disables the only mechanism that would catch child-scope drift for a "none" container
resign.py:237 the unconditional stale-pin-drift invalidation exists only in the resign path, not in compute_validity
dropped.finding: A container whose live direct children all declare file_impact_scope=="none" now signs an attestation with file_scope=="none" and empty deps; at claim-gate validity time this skips BOTH per-dependency re-hashing and the whole-HEAD stale-head fallback, so a child later flipping to scope=="paths" and drifting code does not invalidate the container attestation under the default (enforce_plan_material_pins=False) config — a fail-open regression from the prior fail-closed 'unscoped/any-commit-invalidates' behavior.
scenarios: Container story with two children both declared --none signs at planning time (file_scope=none). A child is later edited to declare file_impact:[{path: src/x.py}] and code in src/x.py is committed/modified. With default config the container attestation remains 'certified' and a claim passes despite the code the plan now depends on having drifted.
